explanation: In the form y = mx + b, the slope is simply the number multiplying x -- you can read it straight off the equation with no graph needed. Slide m and the line tilts; the green run of 1 and violet rise of m form a triangle that proves the slope. The b slider slides the line up and down but never changes how steep it is, so the slope readout only follows m.
bullets: In y = mx + b the slope is m, the coefficient of x.
Stepping 1 to the right makes the line rise by exactly m.
Changing b moves the line up/down but leaves the slope unchanged.
